terms.label: Prototype
terms.definition: An implementation used to test feasibility or an idea.
terms.caveat: It may be disposable and is not necessarily a published release.

terms.label: Pre-Alpha
terms.definition: Early development before the project considers itself ready for alpha testing.
terms.caveat: There is no cross-project entry or exit criterion.

terms.label: Experimental
terms.definition: A feature or build offered for experimentation without a stable commitment.
terms.caveat: This can describe a single feature inside an otherwise stable product.

terms.label: Alpha
terms.definition: An early testing stage with incomplete or changing behavior.
terms.caveat: Feature completeness and support guarantees are project-defined.

terms.label: Beta
terms.definition: A prerelease stage intended to collect feedback and identify defects.
terms.caveat: Feature completeness and production eligibility require a product policy.

terms.label: Preview
terms.definition: An umbrella label for functionality available before its intended general release.
terms.caveat: Preview is not a standardized position between alpha and beta.

terms.label: Developer Preview
terms.definition: An advance release aimed at developers evaluating APIs or integrations.
terms.caveat: It does not by itself promise API compatibility.

terms.label: Technical Preview
terms.definition: An advance technology evaluation made available before a final offering.
terms.caveat: Availability does not imply a production-support commitment.

terms.label: Release Candidate
terms.definition: A build proposed as the final release if acceptance checks reveal no blocking issues.
terms.caveat: An RC is still a prerelease; production support can have explicit exceptions.

terms.label: Stable
terms.definition: A release or channel the project considers suitable for its normal supported use.
terms.caveat: Stable is a project claim, not a guarantee of zero bugs or unchanged behavior.

terms.label: Final
terms.definition: The published outcome of a particular release cycle.
terms.caveat: An ordinary word such as release can also mean any published build.

terms.label: General Availability
terms.definition: A milestone making a product or feature generally available under its published policy.
terms.caveat: Support scope, regions and production eligibility remain vendor-specific.

terms.label: Release to Manufacturing
terms.definition: A traditional milestone when a build is handed off for manufacturing or distribution.
terms.caveat: It need not share the same date as public availability.

terms.label: Canary
terms.definition: An early-feedback channel exposing very recent changes to detect problems quickly.
terms.caveat: A Canary channel and a canary deployment describe different things.

terms.label: Nightly
terms.definition: A build or channel produced on a nightly development schedule.
terms.caveat: The schedule does not certify maturity, and skipped builds are possible.

terms.label: Daily
terms.definition: A build produced on a daily schedule, regardless of the time of day.
terms.caveat: Cadence alone gives no stability guarantee.

terms.label: Snapshot
terms.definition: A captured state of the code or artifacts at a particular point in development.
terms.caveat: Snapshot identifiers and mutability rules vary by ecosystem.

terms.label: Development
terms.definition: A channel following active development before broader stabilization.
terms.caveat: Its relationship to preview or nightly depends on the project.

terms.label: Unstable
terms.definition: A development stream that accepts changes before stable-release qualification.
terms.caveat: The name is not a measured crash rate; Debian has specific usage.

terms.label: Testing
terms.definition: A stream used to evaluate changes before promotion to a stable release.
terms.caveat: Debian Testing is a named distribution, not a generic QA environment.

terms.label: Edge
terms.definition: A label emphasizing access to very recent changes.
terms.caveat: It can be a product name or a publisher-defined channel.

terms.label: Insider
terms.definition: A vendor-branded program offering access to upcoming changes.
terms.caveat: A program can contain several channels with different guarantees.

terms.label: Next
terms.definition: A publisher-defined pointer or channel for upcoming work.
terms.caveat: A next tag can point at any version the publisher chooses.

terms.label: Latest
terms.definition: A publisher-controlled pointer to a selected package version.
terms.caveat: Do not infer highest version, newest timestamp, or stable from the name.

terms.label: Early Access
terms.definition: Access to software or features before their intended general release.
terms.caveat: This describes access timing, not a fixed maturity stage.

terms.label: Private Preview
terms.definition: An advance offering restricted to selected participants.
terms.caveat: Access rules do not establish stability or support.

terms.label: Public Preview
terms.definition: An advance offering open to a broad public audience.
terms.caveat: Public availability is not equivalent to GA.

terms.label: Closed Beta
terms.definition: A beta restricted to an invited or selected audience.
terms.caveat: Closed describes participation, while beta describes the stated stage.

terms.label: Open Beta
terms.definition: A beta made available for public participation.
terms.caveat: Public participation does not guarantee production readiness.

terms.label: Long Term Support
terms.definition: A release with a provider-defined extended maintenance period.
terms.caveat: Duration, patch requirements and covered components vary.

terms.label: Standard Term Support
terms.definition: A standard-duration support track used by products such as .NET.
terms.caveat: It is not a lower-quality maturity tier than LTS.

terms.label: Extended Support Release
terms.definition: A release track designed for a longer maintenance or deployment horizon.
terms.caveat: Its actual lifecycle is product-specific.

terms.label: Extended Stable
terms.definition: A stable track offering a longer interval between some feature updates.
terms.caveat: Slower feature cadence does not mean security updates can be ignored.

terms.label: Interim Release
terms.definition: A release between longer-lived releases, commonly with a shorter support window.
terms.caveat: Interim can be a fully supported stable release.

terms.label: Oldstable
terms.definition: The previous stable release in ecosystems using this label.
terms.caveat: The label alone does not establish whether support is still available.

terms.label: Legacy
terms.definition: An older implementation or release retained for compatibility or migration.
terms.caveat: Legacy has no universal support deadline.

terms.label: Deprecated
terms.definition: A feature, version or practice marked for transition away from continued use.
terms.caveat: Deprecated does not necessarily mean already removed or immediately unsupported.

terms.label: End of Life
terms.definition: The end of a provider-defined lifecycle or support period.
terms.caveat: EOL and end of support may be separate milestones in a specific policy.

terms.label: Rolling Release
terms.definition: A distribution model evolving through a continuous stream of package updates.
terms.caveat: This is separate from rolling deployment and can contain stable packages.

terms.label: Fixed Release
terms.definition: A distribution model organized around discrete named or numbered releases.
terms.caveat: Update and maintenance policies still need to be specified.

terms.label: Release Train
terms.definition: A recurring schedule in which ready work advances through release stages.
terms.caveat: Unready features may wait for a later train.

terms.label: Point Release
terms.definition: An incremental update within an existing release line.
terms.caveat: Some distributions use it for refreshed installation media; it is not always a SemVer patch.

terms.label: Major Release
terms.definition: Under SemVer, an increment communicating incompatible public API changes.
terms.caveat: Other version schemes assign different meanings to major numbers.

terms.label: Minor Release
terms.definition: Under SemVer, an increment for backward-compatible functionality.
terms.caveat: The public API contract determines compatibility.

terms.label: Patch Release
terms.definition: Under SemVer, an increment for backward-compatible bug fixes.
terms.caveat: A small diff does not prove a change is backward compatible.

terms.label: Hotfix
terms.definition: A targeted fix delivered outside or faster than the ordinary release schedule.
terms.caveat: Urgency does not waive verification or determine the version increment.

terms.label: Security Release
terms.definition: An update intended to address security issues.
terms.caveat: It can also be a patch, maintenance release or backport.

terms.label: Maintenance Release
terms.definition: A release focused on sustaining or correcting an existing release line.
terms.caveat: Its exact scope can include more than bug fixes.

terms.label: Service Pack
terms.definition: A packaged collection of updates for a product release.
terms.caveat: This is a vendor-specific packaging convention.

terms.label: Backport
terms.definition: A change adapted from a newer development line to an older one.
terms.caveat: Backport describes the adaptation, not a maturity stage or complete release.

terms.label: Prerelease
terms.definition: Under SemVer, a version carrying a hyphen-prefixed prerelease identifier.
terms.caveat: It has lower precedence than the corresponding normal version.

terms.label: Build Metadata
terms.definition: Under SemVer, plus-prefixed metadata attached to a version.
terms.caveat: Build metadata does not affect version precedence.

terms.label: Semantic Versioning
terms.definition: A specification relating version numbers to a declared public API.
terms.caveat: It does not define Canary, Preview, LTS or deployment strategies.

terms.label: Canary Deployment
terms.definition: A deployment that initially exposes a new version to a limited audience or traffic share.
terms.caveat: It can deploy a stable build and does not define a release channel.

terms.label: Blue/Green Deployment
terms.definition: A deployment approach using separate old and new environments to switch traffic.
terms.caveat: Database changes and shared state need their own transition plan.

terms.label: Rolling Deployment
terms.definition: A deployment that replaces instances in successive groups.
terms.caveat: Old and new versions may run together; this is separate from rolling release.

terms.label: Feature Flag
terms.definition: A control allowing selected behavior to be enabled separately from distributing the code.
terms.caveat: A flag is not a substitute for compatibility and lifecycle policy.
